title.narrative: SUNDAR SHAKTI: An innovation towards Climate Adaptation and Livelihood Security through Women-led Solar Energy and NbS

description.narrative:
Mousuni Island, located in the Namkhana block of South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, is one of the most climate-vulnerable regions in India. It faces recurrent cyclones, tidal surges, flooding, and saline intrusion—leading to massive disruption in electricity supply, degradation of soil productivity, loss of livelihoods, and forced migration. The socio-economic impact is disproportionately high on women, marginal farmers, and landless communities. Despite various governmental and non-governmental initiatives, sustainable and resilient livelihood options remain limited. The “Sundar Shakti” concept emerges as an innovative response to this challenge. It proposes a decentralized, women-led, solar-powered energy model integrated with nature-based solutions (NbS) to build long-term climate resilience. The model aims to empower women (especially Solar Sakhis) as agents of change who can manage solar microgrids and promote climate-adaptive livelihoods. The proposed innovation links energy access with livelihood diversification through activities like vetiver plantation, organic farming, and mangrove restoration—creating an ecosystem of resilience, enterprise, and empowerment.
This scoping study, under the ITL initiative, seeks to assess the feasibility of this integrated approach. It will analyse the social, technical, financial, and environmental viability of implementing the model at scale, while also exploring the enabling ecosystem required to support community ownership, sustainability, and institutional convergence.
About the partner: Calcutta Society for Professional Action in Development (SPADE) was founded in 1994 by a group of development professionals from a diverse field basically to provide techno-managerial support to other organizations operating in the development sector. Over time, SPADE has emerged as a prominent professional organization having an outstanding capacity in providing consultancy services as well as in conducting various Studies, Researches and documentations related to the field of development. All SPADE people have distinct technical-professional expertise in diverse fields which converged in its work. SPADE is member of the West Bengal Self Help Group Promotional Forum – a State level network of Self Help Promoting Institutions in West Bengal since its inception in 2001 and a member of the State Inter Agency Group – West Bengal that was formed in mid 2000 initially to avert the type of devastation caused by exceptionally widespread floods of West Bengal in 2000 and gradually it emerged as a collective effort of promoting the core concept of unified humanitarian response across the state.
